NextItNet’s residual dilated causal convolutions provide a structural reference for attribution: for stride-one layers, receptive-field width is R = 1 + Σℓ(kℓ−1)dℓ, counting every convolution. This bounds possible influence; measured perturbation sensitivity estimates actual influence. The 2024 paper [Measuring Recency Bias](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.09722) cautions that excessive recent-item dependence can also hurt accuracy. The 2025 [counterfactual explanation study](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.03606) searches discrete history edits that change recommendations; [TRACE (2026)](https://github.com/devUuung/TRACE) explicitly targets ranking-aware counterfactual explanations. These support diagnostic history edits without replacing or retraining the backbone. Architecture reference: [NextItNet](https://fajieyuan.github.io/papers/nextitnet6.pdf).

Practical synthesis: freeze the single trained model and candidate set; compare equal-size deletions of recent coherent interactions, older isolated interactions, and random interactions. Define coherence using observed title/description similarity, with timestamp gaps as supplementary evidence. Compact surviving interactions, left-pad again, and read the final nonpadding position. Shuffle only valid items; separately shuffle the prefix while retaining the last item to distinguish order dependence from last-item identity dependence. Report paired target-rank changes, score-margin changes, and hit@10 flips. Deletions shift surviving positions, so use same-position item replacements as complementary controls. These are model-sensitivity probes, not identified causal effects on user preferences.

Synthetic controls should test the implementation directly: changing future tokens must leave earlier features unchanged; replacing tokens outside the theoretical receptive field must leave the selected feature unchanged, assuming no global temporal operations. Exercise short left-padded histories to catch count−1 readout errors. Evaluate with dropout disabled; repeat random perturbations and bootstrap paired user-level differences within each category, then macro-average, reporting 95% intervals. Older-item sensitivity exceeding recent-item sensitivity suggests stale dependence only after matching deletion size, coherence, and receptive-field eligibility.
